title: Space constructibility of logarithmic space
statement: Define $L(n)=1+\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ for $n\ge 1$, and set $L(0)=1$. There are a positive integer $c$ and a finite binary Turing machine that, on every binary input $x$, outputs the binary representation of $L(|x|)$ and uses at most $cL(|x|)$ work-tape cells; moreover, $L(n)\le L(n)$ for every $n\in\mathbb N$.
hypotheses_covered: For every natural number n, the logarithmic-space function at n is at most itself
